# User guide: Config Hub

## In plain words

Each AI agent keeps its settings in its own file, in its own format. Without help, you would add the same tool or the same instructions to many files by hand. The Config Hub keeps one shared copy of four things: MCP servers (tools that an agent can call), global instructions, skills and commands. You choose which agents receive each item. When you press **Apply to agents**, the Config Hub writes the item into the file of each chosen agent, in the format that the agent reads. If you edit one of those files by hand, the Config Hub notices and asks you what to do. It never overwrites your edit without asking. The Config Hub can also keep a history of your settings, so that you can look back and restore an earlier version.

Words used on this page:

- **MCP server**: a program or web service that gives an agent extra tools.
- **Skill**: a folder of instructions, with one main file called SKILL.md, that an agent loads when it needs it.
- **Command**: a saved prompt that you start with a slash, for example /review.
- **Projection**: the step that writes the shared copy into the file of one agent. The button for it is **Apply to agents**.
- **Drift**: a difference between what the Config Hub wrote and what the file holds now, because someone edited the file.

## Where to find it

1. Open **Settings** in the Unraid WebGUI.
2. Open **AI CLI Agents**.
3. Press the **Config Hub** tab.

The tab has four cards in this order: **MCP Servers**, **Global Instructions**, **Skills & Commands** and **History**. A card called **Config drift detected** appears above them only when a file has drifted. Each card has a header row with a status line, such as "2 servers · on", "64 KB · 11 agents", "0 skills · 0 commands" or "last commit 2 h ago". The (i) button of a card explains the card in a few short sentences. Press the name of a card to close it or open it. The **...** button moves it. **Reset layout** at the top of the tab puts the cards back in the default order. The page remembers the order and the open cards in this browser only.

If the agent home is not mounted, a banner says so. You can still edit the shared copies. **Apply to agents** does not work until a workspace or the array brings the home online. The Config Hub never writes into an unmounted home.

Each tile in a list of agents shows the agent name and the path of the file that the Config Hub would write. The whole tile is the check box: you can press anywhere on it, and it is at least 44 px tall on a phone. An agent that is not installed shows dimmed with the tag **not installed**. You cannot select it.

## Which agents receive what

The table shows what each agent can receive. "Yes" means the Config Hub can write that item for the agent. "No" means the agent has no file that the Config Hub can use.

| Agent | MCP servers | Global instructions | Skills | Commands |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Claude Code | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Gemini CLI | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes (converted to the Gemini format) |
| Antigravity CLI | Yes | Yes (same file as Gemini CLI) | Yes | No |
| Qwen Code | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| OpenCode | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Kilo Code | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| GitHub Copilot | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Codex CLI | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Goose | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Factory CLI | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Grok Build | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Kimi Code | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Pi Coder | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| NanoCoder | Yes | No | No | No |

Notes on the table:

- **Pi Coder has no MCP support.** The author of Pi Coder chose not to add it. The Config Hub does not pretend that it does.
- **NanoCoder** reads only files inside a project folder, not global files. The Config Hub does not write into a project folder.
- **Grok Build** reads the instruction file of a project, not a global one. It receives skills and commands.
- **Codex CLI** has no commands in the Config Hub, because Codex uses skills in place of commands.
- **Antigravity CLI** and **Gemini CLI** read the same instruction file. If you select either one, the Config Hub writes that file once.
- **Five agents share one skills folder:** Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Goose read the same shared folder. The Config Hub writes it once. It keeps the files while any of the five is still selected.
- The MCP file formats differ. Most agents use JSON. Codex CLI and Grok Build use TOML. Goose uses YAML. The Config Hub writes each one in the format of the agent.

## How to use it

### Add an MCP server

1. In the **MCP Servers** card, press **Add Server**.
2. Type a **Name**. Use letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters.
3. Choose a **Transport**.
   - **stdio (local command)**: a program that runs on the Unraid server.
   - **http (streamable HTTP)** or **sse (server-sent events)**: a web address of a remote server.
4. For stdio, type the **Command** (the full path of the program). Type the **Arguments**, one on each line.
5. For http or sse, type the **URL**, including `https://`. Then choose **Authentication** if the server needs a login (see "Log in to a remote server" below).
6. For a stdio server, add **Environment variables** if the program needs them. Press **Add variable** for each one.
7. Under **Enable for agents**, tick each agent that should receive this server.
8. Press **Save Server**.

Expect: the server shows in the list, with a chip for each agent that you ticked. A server with no ticked agent shows "no agents targeted".

At this point nothing has changed in any agent file. The server is only stored.

An environment variable can hold the text `{SECRET_KEY}`. At **Apply to agents**, the Config Hub replaces it with the value of that key from your secrets (see [Agent Store](agent-store.md)). The Config Hub keeps the placeholder in its own copy. After you save, the values of environment variables show masked.

To change a server, press the pencil icon. To remove one, press the trash icon. A removed server leaves the agent files at the next **Apply to agents**.

### Log in to a remote server

A remote server (http or sse) often wants a login. The editor has an **Authentication** choice and a list of **Additional headers**. A header is a named line that the agent sends with each request to the server.

1. Store the secret first. In the Agent Store, open the **Variables** panel of any agent, press **Add secret**, and give the secret a name in capital letters, for example `MY_TOKEN` (see [Agent Store](agent-store.md)). The plugin keeps each secret once, by its name.
2. In the editor, choose **Bearer token** and type the key in braces: `{MY_TOKEN}`. The Config Hub adds `Bearer ` in front for you.
3. Choose **Custom header** when the server wants another header, for example `X-API-Key`. Type the header name and the value `{MY_KEY}`.
4. Under **Additional headers**, press **Add header** for a header that is not a login, for example a tenant number. This kind of value can be plain text.
5. Press **Save Server**.

The Config Hub never stores a typed token. A header that carries a login must hold a key in braces. If you type the token itself, the editor and the Config Hub refuse it and tell you to store the secret first. The reason is that the shared copy is a plain file, and the history backup would copy it. At **Apply to agents**, the Config Hub puts the real value into the file of each agent, in the form that the agent reads. The shared copy and the history keep only the key in braces.

The same rule holds for a variable of a local server whose name looks like a login (for example a name with `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `KEY`), and for a web address that has a login in it, for example `?api_key=...`. Write `{MY_KEY}` in place of the value. If you use **Adopt** on a file that holds the real value of one of your secrets, the Config Hub puts the key in braces back for you. The drift list never shows a real secret value.

#### A server that you saved before this rule

An older server can still hold a typed login. Each later change to it is refused, for example **Save Server**, a change of the agent ticks, or the on and off switch. The message ends with the steps to take. It also shows the button **Move to the secrets vault**. Press the button. The Config Hub puts each typed login into the secrets vault under a new name, such as `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`, and keeps only that name in braces in the server. If the vault already holds the same value, the Config Hub uses that name. The message lists the places and the vault names, and never a value. Then press **Apply to agents**.

If a key in braces is not in your secrets, the editor warns you after you save. The agent would receive the text `{MY_TOKEN}` and the server would reject it.

After you save, the values of headers show masked. Leave a masked value as it is to keep it.

### Test the connection

Press **Test connection** in the editor to check a remote server before you apply it.

1. Fill in the **URL** and the **Authentication**. You do not need to save first.
2. Press **Test connection**.

Expect: a green line such as "Connected (HTTP 200), 2 tools." or a red line with the HTTP status and a short reason, for example "HTTP 401: the server rejected the request as unauthenticated."

Facts about the test:

- The Unraid server makes the request, not your browser. It can reach any address that the Unraid server can reach, including your local network. Only a signed-in administrator can start it.
- The test uses only http and https. It does not follow a redirect. It stops after 5 seconds to connect, 10 seconds for each request and 1 MB of reply.
- The result shows the status code and a fixed reason. It never shows the text that the remote server sent.
- The test does not save anything.

### Switch a server off and on

Each server row has a button that reads **On** or **Off**.

1. Press **On** to switch the server off for all agents. The button then reads **Off**. The row is dimmed and shows the badge **off**.
2. Press **Off** to switch the server on again.

The Config Hub keeps your choice of agents when a server is off. A switched-off server leaves the agent files at the next **Apply to agents**. When you switch it on and apply again, it returns to the same agents. Editing the server does not change the switch.

### Apply to agents

1. Press **Apply to agents**.

Expect: a box under the button lists each file with the counts, for example `.gemini/settings.json — 1 written, 0 removed`. If nothing needed a change, the box reads "All agent configs already up to date."

The tab has three **Apply to agents** buttons, one in each of the first three cards. Each button runs the same projection for all items. The result shows under the button that you pressed. The **Global Instructions** button also saves your text and your ticked agents first.

The Config Hub only touches the entries that it manages. An MCP server that you added by hand in an agent file stays as it is. If a file cannot be read, for example because it has a syntax error, the Config Hub leaves the file unchanged and reports the failure.

### When an agent picks it up

An agent reads its files when it starts. A workspace that is already running keeps its old configuration.

- A new workspace, or a workspace that you restart, uses the new configuration.
- After **Apply to agents**, the result box lists the running workspaces of each changed agent, with the text "has running session(s) — reload to pick up the new config". Each line has a **Reload agent** button.
- **Reload agent** stops the agent in that workspace and starts it again, so that it reads the files. The button then reads "Reload sent".

> [!WARNING]
> **Reload agent** interrupts the work in progress in that workspace. Press it only when the agent is idle. The Config Hub never restarts a workspace by itself.

### Drift: Adopt, Overwrite or Release

When a file differs from what the Config Hub wrote, the banner **Config drift detected** shows one row for each key. The row shows the file, the key, and the kind of difference in brackets.

| Kind | What it means |
| :-- | :-- |
| modified | Someone changed the value in the file. |
| deleted | Someone removed an entry that the Config Hub manages. |
| unmanaged_conflict | The file already had an entry with the same name, which the Config Hub did not write. |
| write_failed | The Config Hub could not write the file, so it left it alone. The row names the reason, for example that the file has comments or a trailing comma (the Config Hub cannot rewrite such a file without losing them), that a link points nowhere, or that a folder is not writable. |

Press **show values** to compare what is on disk with the value in the Config Hub.

Choose one button for each row.

| Button | What it does | What is kept |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Adopt** | Takes the value from the file into the Config Hub. The Config Hub copy now matches your edit. | Your edit. |
| **Overwrite** | Writes the Config Hub value back over your edit. A box asks you to confirm. | The Config Hub value. Your edit is lost. |
| **Release** | Stops managing this key. The Config Hub leaves the file as it is. It also removes the agent from the targets of that server, so that the next **Apply to agents** does not take the key back. | Your edit stays in the file. |

For a file that the Config Hub writes as one managed block, **Adopt** does not work. This applies to the Codex CLI and Goose files, and to the instruction files. The Config Hub cannot read your edit back into separate keys. Use **Overwrite** or **Release** for those rows.

The Codex CLI and Goose files hold the managed block beside your own entries. If you wrote an entry with the same name outside the block, the Config Hub does not write a second one, because the agent would refuse the file. The row shows the kind **unmanaged_conflict** and the text "Defined outside the managed block". **Overwrite** also refuses. Rename or remove your entry in the file, then press **Apply to agents**.

On a row for the Relay guidance, the Relay skill or the Plugin management skill, **Release** only stops the Config Hub from tracking that row. It never changes the agent ticks that you chose for your own instructions and skills. **Adopt** takes an edited OpenCode or Kilo entry into the Config Hub, including its arguments and variables.

### Global instructions

The **Global Instructions** card holds one document. The Config Hub writes it into the instruction file of each agent that you tick. Every ticked agent loads it at the start of a session.

1. Press **Edit** in the header of the card. The text box opens (it is closed at first). Type or paste the text. The size shows under it, with a limit of 262144 bytes (256 KB). The status line of the card shows the size and the number of ticked agents.
2. Under **Project to agents**, tick the agents that should receive the text. Nothing is ticked by default.
3. Press **Apply to agents**.

Expect: the Config Hub saves the text and your choices, then writes the files. An Unraid notification lists the change for each agent.

There is no separate **Save** button. Ticking an agent also saves the document and the choice at once.

The Config Hub keeps your own text safe:

- For most agents, it writes the document inside a marked block in the instruction file. Text outside the block is never touched.
- Claude Code and Kilo Code read every file in a rules folder. The Config Hub writes its own file there and never edits your personal instruction file of Claude Code. Claude Code gets a short line that points to the one shared copy, so the text stays in one place.
- An empty document removes the block at the next **Apply to agents**.
- A document that contains the marker text of a block is refused.

### Skills and commands

The **Skills & Commands** card has two lists side by side.

To add a skill:

1. Press **Add Skill**.
2. Type a **Skill name**. It becomes the folder name inside each agent. Use letters, digits, `_` and `-`.
3. Write the file `SKILL.md`. A skill must have it.
4. Press **Add file** to add other files to the skill, if you need them.
5. Press **Save Skill**.

To add a command:

1. Press **Add Command**.
2. Type a **Command name**. The Config Hub stores it as `<name>.md`.
3. Write the full text of the command in markdown. This is what the agent reads when someone runs it.
4. Press **Save Command**.

Then choose where they go. Under **Project skills to** and **Project commands to**, tick the agents. The page saves each tick at once, but nothing is written to an agent until you press **Apply to agents**. The lists of agents differ, because not every agent has both items (see the table above).

When you remove a skill or a command, or a file from a skill, the Config Hub copy goes at once. The copies in the agents go at the next **Apply to agents**.

The Config Hub only touches the copies that it wrote. A skill or command that you placed in an agent folder yourself is never changed or removed. If one of your files has the same name as a Config Hub item, the Config Hub reports a conflict and does not overwrite it.

## The Relay guidance that the Config Hub installs by default

Some guidance does not need a tick. The Config Hub writes it for every agent that has a place for it.

| Item | What it tells the agent | Which agents |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Relay guidance | How to use the Agent Relay: read the inbox, send a message to a topic or a workspace, treat a message as data. | Every agent with a global instruction file (all agents in the table that show "Yes" under global instructions). |
| Relay skill | The same Relay rules, as a skill. | Every agent that can read skills. Grok Build gets the skill, because it has no global instruction file. NanoCoder gets nothing. |
| File-path rule | Write a file name in a form that the terminal can turn into a link. | The same agents as the Relay guidance. |
| Voice and Notebook paragraphs | When to speak to you, and when to put a page in the Notebook. | Added to the Relay guidance only when **Let agents manage the plugin** is on, and the matching feature (**Voice** or **Notebook**) is on. |

Facts about this guidance:

- Claude Code and Kilo Code get their own files in their rules folders. Other agents get a marked block inside the one instruction file that they read.
- When you switch **Let agents manage the plugin**, **Voice** or **Notebook** on or off, the Config Hub updates the text at once. The next session of an agent reads the new text.
- If you edit inside a marked block, the next projection puts the text back. Write your own text outside the block.
- The Relay tools themselves, and the check box **Give agents built-in Relay tools**, are on the **Agent Relay** tab (see [Agent Relay](relay.md)). Every agent also reaches the Relay through the command in its shell, without any setting.

## Settings backup with git (the History card)

The **History** card keeps versions of your agent configuration with git (the common version control tool). It is off until you turn it on.

### Turn it on

1. Check that git is installed on the server. If it is not, the card says "git is not installed on this server" and tells you to install git with NerdTools from Community Applications. The plugin does not include git.
2. Press **Enable config backup**.
3. Read the box and press **Enable**.

Expect: the card shows a status line, for example "Backup enabled — 3 commits · working tree clean · auto-commit on (30 s debounce)".

The button is grey while the agent home is not mounted.

### What the backup holds

- The Config Hub store: your MCP servers, instructions, skills and commands.
- The files that the Config Hub writes into the agent home.
- Your list of workspaces.
- A copy of three small plugin settings files: the main settings, the version pins of the agents, and the list of your own secret names.

The backup lists the allowed files and leaves out everything else. It never holds login files. Examples are the main file of Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`), the Gemini token file and the Codex login file. It never holds your secrets file. When a projected file holds a secret value that came from your secrets, the commit keeps the `{KEY}` placeholder and not the value.

### Use the history

A commit is one saved version. The Config Hub commits by itself, about 30 seconds after the last change. It groups changes that come close together into one commit.

- **Commit now** saves a version at once. You can type a short message. Use file names only. Never type a secret.
- The timeline shows the last 20 commits. Press a commit to open it. It lists the files that changed.
- **Diff** on a file shows how the file now differs from that commit. This is what **Restore** would change back.
- **Restore** on a file sets that file back to the content of that commit. The restore is a commit too, so you can undo it. If you changed the file in the last 30 seconds, the Config Hub saves that change as its own commit first, so it is not lost. A second restore of the same version also answers "ok".
- **Restore settings** (at the top of the card) copies the plugin settings from the last backup back over the live settings. The box names them: the main settings, the version pins and the list of secret names. Workspaces and the agent home are not touched. Reload the page afterwards.

> [!WARNING]
> **Restore settings** overwrites your live plugin settings with the last committed backup. Any change you made after that backup is lost. **Restore** on a file overwrites the current content of that file.

If a bake (a save of the home to storage) is running, a commit or a restore answers "Busy". Try again in a moment.

### Push to a remote server

You can send the history to a git server that you control. Nothing is ever sent unless you press **Push**.

1. Under **Remote backup**, type the **Remote URL**, for example `https://github.com/you/agent-config.git`.
2. Type the **Access token**. The field is masked. You can press the eye icon to check what you typed.
3. Press **Save remote**.
4. Press **Push**.

Expect: a box reads "Config backup pushed to the remote."

Rules for the remote:

- Do not put your token in the URL. A URL with `user:token@` is refused.
- Use `https`. An `http` address saves, but with a warning, because it sends the token in clear text.
- The token is kept in your secrets, under the name `HUB_GIT_TOKEN`. The plugin passes it to git in a safe way and never shows it again.
- **Push** stays grey until a remote URL and a token are saved.

### If the backup stops saving

The status line turns red and reads "Backup is NOT saving", followed by the reason. A git repository that is damaged in the agent home repairs itself at the next commit. The history before the damage may be lost, but your files are safe.

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Enable for agents** (on a server) | The agents that receive this MCP server. | None | Tick the agents that need the server. |
| **Project to agents** (instructions) | The agents that receive the global instructions. | None | Tick the agents that should follow the shared text. |
| **Project skills to**, **Project commands to** | The agents that receive skills and commands. | None | Tick the agents that have the surface. |
| **Enable config backup** | Turns on the git history. | Off | Turn it on when you want to look back or restore. |
| Auto-commit | A commit about 30 seconds after a change. | On, once the backup is enabled | Use **Commit now** when you want a version at once. |
| **Remote URL** and **Access token** | The git server for **Push**. | Empty | Set them when you want an offsite copy. |

## What happens behind the scenes

The Config Hub keeps its store in the agent home, in a folder that is part of the home layers. A projector (the part that writes one agent's file) compares three values for each key: what the Config Hub wrote last time, what the file holds now, and what the Config Hub wants now. When the first two differ, it reports drift and does not write. For the technical description, see C4 Component: Config Env Secrets.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The banner "The agent home is not mounted". | The home layers are not mounted. Nothing is written. | Open a workspace, or start the array. Then press **Apply to agents**. |
| An agent tile is dimmed with **not installed**. | The agent is not installed. | Install it in the Agent Store (see [Agent Store](agent-store.md)). |
| A running agent does not show the change. | The agent read its files at start. | Restart the workspace, or press **Reload agent** when the agent is idle. |
| **Config drift detected**. | Someone edited a managed file. | Choose **Adopt**, **Overwrite** or **Release** for each key. |
| **Adopt** says it cannot work. | The file is a managed block. | Use **Overwrite** or **Release**. |
| "The MCP server list (mcp.json) cannot be read" or "The Config Hub state (state.json) cannot be read". | The file is damaged, for example by a merge conflict. The Config Hub changed nothing and kept a copy next to the file, named with `.corrupt-` and a time. | Repair the file, or delete it to start with an empty list. Then press **Apply to agents**. |
| "Projection failed". | A file could not be read or written. | Read the message. Fix the file, or choose **Overwrite**. |
| The skill is refused with "SKILL.md required". | A skill must have a main file. | Add the file `SKILL.md`. |
| "git is not installed on this server". | The History card needs git. | Install git with NerdTools. |
| "Backup is NOT saving". | A commit failed. | Read the reason in the status line. Press **Commit now** to try again. |
| **Push** is grey. | No remote URL or no token is saved. | Fill in both and press **Save remote**. |
| "Push failed". | The remote refused the push or cannot be reached. | Check the URL, the token and the network. |
